headline: Approved a $1,500.00 donation for 2026; no other votes were recorded.
summary: The meeting covered library programs, visitor and checkout numbers, and two new state laws. It also covered the Friends group's annual report and fundraising. The only recorded decision was approval of a $1,500.00 donation for 2026.
plain_text:
8/6/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Lauren Read, Dana Visser, Jessica Wignal, Colleen Moore, Prudence 
Doherty
City Staff Present: Ray Coffey, Nate Eddy
Guests Present: Rachel Moreau
Call to Order by: Prudence
Meeting Start Time: 6:35 PM
Minutes Recorded by: Lauren
Public Comment
No members of the public present.
Committee Member Updates
Welcome back Jess!
Lauren has moved to South Burlington but will continue serving on the committee.
Library Updates
Programming: 
l Programming had largely been on hiatus in May, however resumed on June 13 for our 
reopening celebration with a visit from Audubon! 
l As we move into summer, our 10-week reading challenge is open for youth to 
participate and kids can track their own participation. This year’s theme is “unearth a 
story” and is heavy on dinosaur and fossil activities.  
l Additionally, Kirsten has resumed storytimes and playgroups on Tuesdays and 
Thursdays, STEAM programming on Saturdays, craft & art making, and food challenges 
for both teens and youth. 
l Partnerships continue to support programming with Audubon VT, CSWD, Lake 
Champlain Basin Program, and Old Spokes Home.  
l On the adult side, we have resumed book club(s) and our monthly writing group and 
finished the last veggie distribution in partnership with Intervale which we are hoping to 
start up again in the fall.  
l The library was the recipient of a VT Humanities award to host a book discussion of the 
graphic novel Charity & Sylvia by Tillie Walden on July 28. This was facilitated by Peter 
Burns and 25 copies of the title were given to us for distribution. 
Statistics:
l Since reopening, our overall, circ, door count, and registration numbers are all trending 
upward.  
l Circulation: 637 (May) & 1033 (June) & 1600 (July) 
l Door count: 87 (May) & 748 (June) & 1022 (July) 
l E-circ: 926 (May) & 890 (June) & 998 (July) 
l July saw our highest totals historically for print & e-circ!
l 134 new library card registrations 
l Seeing considerably less use of public PCs in the new space
Friends of the Winooski Library:
l The Friends held their first book sale outside the library on Saturday, June 13. Over 
$500 was raised from the event! The next scheduled sale will be at the farmer’s market 
on Sunday, August 23.  
l To date, ~$500 has also been raised from the Bookstall at Scout. 
General: 
l Nate & Kirsten attended this year’s Vermont Library Association conference at UVM. 
Both attended helpful workshops, including the Silver Special Collections Open House led 
by our very own Prudence! 
l S.232 was signed into law by Gov. Scott. As a reminder, the bill amends the statutes 
related to libraries and education grants;  to designate the third Monday in October as 
Vermont Libraries Day; to expressly include public libraries in the list of eligible recipients 
of afterschool and summer reading funding from the Universal Afterschool and Summer 
Special Fund; to expressly include public libraries in the list of community organizations 
eligible for early education funding; to modify the term “collection” to include digital or 
physical materials wherever that term is used in the statute governing the duties of the 
Department of Libraries; and to require the Department of Libraries to publish guidance 
documents concerning grants and funding available to municipal public libraries, and 
expressly authorize municipalities to bond for improvements to any public library. 
l Act 150., an act relating to prohibiting civil arrest in sensitive locations, has been signed 
by Gov. Phil Scott. As written, “sensitive locations” include public libraries and by 
definition, “Civil arrest” means an arrest for purposes of obtaining a person’s presence or 
attendance at a civil proceeding, including an immigration proceeding. 
l The act does not include cases / protections for treason, felony, or breach of the 
peace.
FY26 Review
FY25*^ vs. FY26~ Statistics
l Door Count: +14.3% (8,171 vs. 9,342) 
l New Card Registration: -1.6% (443 vs. 436) 
l Print Circulation: +60.7% (7,919 vs. 12,722) 
l Digital Circulation: +7.1% (9,921 vs. 10,622) 
l Programs: +10.8% (287 vs. 318) 
l Programming Attendance: +27.9% (2,609 vs. 3,336)
*Library temporarily relocated to the O’Brien Community Center September – November 2025
^Youth services coordinator on leave September – December 2025
~Closed May 4 – June 11, 2026
Friends of The Winooski Library
Friends of the Winooski Library
2025–2026 Annual Report (Quick Version)
Friends Board: Rachel Moreau (President), Cathy McIsaac (Secretary), Emily Stoneking 
(Treasurer),
Llewellyn Powell (Book Sales), Katie Livermore (Community Engagement), Sara DeFilippi 
(General/Event
Support), and Kate Statell (General/Event Support)
Organizational Milestones
? Expanded and complete board: 7* (Sara DeFilippi to be confirmed at August meeting)
? New Members: 56
? Updated Bylaws
? Signed MOU with Winooski Memorial Library
? New Registered Agent, professional service with Harbor Compliance
2025–2026 Events
? August 10, 2025 – Outreach tabling at the Winooski Farmers Market
? October 25, 2025 – Fall Book Donation Drive
? November 1, 2025 – Two board members attended Vermont Libraries Friends Fall Forum
? December 4, 2025 – Outreach tabling at the Winooski Holiday Pop-up
? March 28, 2026 – Spring Book Donation Drive
? June 13, 2026 – Friends Summer Sidewalk Sale
Outreach and Communications
? Launched monthly Group Chat & newsletter
? Created new website – WinooskiLibraryFriends.org
? Created new Instagram – Winooski Library Friends
Fundraising & Financials
? Friends Tiny Bookshop: $500
? Friends Summer Sidewalk Sale: $500
? Individual donations: $200
? Applied for City Market Rally for Change program
Available Funds $3,808.29
Approved 2026 Donation $1,500.00
Question about investing available funds to grow interest and Rachel said she would look into it.
Other Business
No building updates other than the project continues to move forward. Met with the architects 
and the capital campaign is slow but steady.
Adjourn
Motion by: Prudence
Second: Colleen
Meeting End Time: 7:25 PM
I.

V.

VII.
VIII.
